newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Cyclonic storm nears Bangladesh coast.
newsitem.headline: Cyclonic storm nears Bangladesh coast.

text.p: Bangladesh on Sunday alerted police and civil volunteers to stand by for emergency evacuation and relief service as a cyclonic storm headed for the coast from the Bay of Bengal.

The storm, 600 km (370 miles) southwest of Chittagong at 9 a.m. (0300 GMT), was racing towards land and might hit shore early on Monday at speeds of 120 kph (75 mph) or more, weather officials said. The storm, which on Saturday appeared headed for the coast of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, could trigger waves up to six feet (two metres), they said.
Chittagong's port authority has asked all ships to move to outer anchorage to minimise damage from collision in case the storm hits.
"We are taking all precautions although we still hope the cyclone will pass Bangladesh coast towards Burma's Akyab province," one port official said.
All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern part of the Bay of Bengal have been advised to remain close to the coast and take shelter.
A similar storm early last month devastated the Andhra Pradesh coast, killing 971 people.
Bangladesh's worst cyclone in 1991 killed more than 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
